headline: Outflow estimates went from $2.53B to $5.57B in 33 minutes; Binance has confirmed none
dek: Loss figures were on-chain estimates posted within minutes, and the biggest drew the most engagement. The net-exposure estimate and Binance's frozen-funds figures came later and reached a fraction of the audience.

key_numbers.label: engagements on the ~$1B net estimate and CZ's reply to it

narrative: Most of the audience saw the largest loss figure in circulation; Binance has confirmed none. In the sampled posts, 81 cited a loss between $5.5B and $5.9B and drew 8.5M engagements. @0xngmi's roughly $1B net-of-freezes estimate drew 621K, and CZ's 22:23 quote of it 926K, about 1.5M together: more than five to one in favor of the bigger numbers.

The number more than doubled in 33 minutes. At 20:39 UTC @bwenews posted that a Binance hot wallet 'looks to be getting drained for about $2.53B', marked unconfirmed (177K). @DarkWebInformer had $2.77B at 20:54 (176K), @officer_secret about $3.5B 'across multiple chains' at 20:56 (204K), and @WazzCrypto 'at least $5.57B across 3 chains' at 21:12 (226K). Each was an on-chain tally of outflows. Compiled estimates range from about $2.8B on Ethereum alone (CryptoTicker) to $5.8B (Conor Grogan), with @KobeissiLetter's running total reaching about $5.9B at 22:59.

Reach arrived with the large aggregators. @WatcherGuru's 21:42 'Binance hacked with over $5.6 billion stolen' drew 1.98M; @KobeissiLetter's 21:58 post on '-$5.7 billion' of outflows drew 2.22M and was among the few to add 'if confirmed'. Elon Musk's 22:33 'Everyday is Zeroday' (2.1M) quoted the Kobeissi post, putting $5.7B in front of his audience. The figures were repeated in Arabic (@Eyaaaad, 359K; @AZK_SA, 240K) and Japanese (@coinspace_, 219K).

The net estimate, which assumes frozen funds are recovered, reached fewer people. At 21:26 @0xngmi posted (621K) that with USDT and USDC frozen 'the total loss now is around ~1bn', about 0.69 percent of Binance's $144B in custody. CZ quoted it at 22:23: 'Loss might be a bit higher than that, but will cover' (926K). It carried no number, and @KobeissiLetter's 22:59 post (244K) folded it into a running total of '~$5.9 billion'.
Freeze figures drifted the same way. Tether's freeze, first reported by @TreeNewsFeed at ~$971M (21:05), became more than 1.567B USDT per Tether's CEO at 21:25, and posts circulated a combined $1.8B.

Binance's own numbers came last. At 23:22 it said the 'current verified total frozen is $2.54 billion', addressing the $1.8B figure (529K), 100 minutes after @WatcherGuru's $5.6B post. At 00:52 it said 'around $3 billion' (156K). Together those drew 685K, about 16 percent of the 4.2M on the two largest loss-figure posts. Binance has stated frozen amounts and said it will cover losses; it has not published a loss figure.

callouts.title: Cite the source and the minute
callouts.body: Every gross loss figure that night was an outflow estimate, from about $2.5B to $5.9B depending on who counted and when. Gross outflow and net loss after freezes are different numbers. Binance's only stated figures are frozen amounts: $2.54B at 23:22 and around $3B at 00:52.

callouts.title: A lower estimate needs its own number
callouts.body: The net-loss frame peaked with CZ's 22:23 quote, which said only 'a bit higher than that'. Without a figure it was absorbed into larger running totals within 36 minutes. A verified number, posted early, is what competes with the biggest estimate.

watch: A loss figure from Binance or its post-mortem: the first confirmed number resets this ledger and tests whether corrections travel.
